overview: The Medford Bicycle Advisory Commission met informally without a quorum to discuss upcoming city bike infrastructure projects, regional path studies, Bluebikes expansion, and community outreach events.

items.title: Remote Meeting Announcement
items.summary: Denis MacDougall read the state statutory authorization allowing public bodies to hold fully remote meetings.

items.title: Call to Order and Roll Call
items.summary: Jared Powell called the meeting to order, and Daniel Nuzzo-Mueller conducted roll call, noting the commission was one member short of a quorum.

items.title: Website Domain Renewal
items.summary: Pat reported that the commission's website domain was successfully renewed for a ten-year term.

items.title: High Street and Boston Avenue Traffic Calming
items.summary: The commission discussed neighborhood feedback and temporary traffic-calming cones deployed near the intersection of High Street and Boston Avenue.

items.title: Mystic River Path to Minuteman Bikeway Feasibility Study
items.summary: Commission members reviewed Arlington's feasibility study connecting the Mystic River Path to the Minuteman Bikeway and shared design feedback regarding bridge access and rotaries.

items.title: Farmers Market Group Rides and Outreach
items.summary: Leah and Pat detailed plans for neighborhood group rides to the farmers market and joint tabling materials prepared with Walk Medford and Bike to the Sea.

items.title: City Infrastructure Projects and Bluebikes Expansion
items.summary: Amy Ingalls provided status updates on Winthrop Street bike lanes, South Street contraflow finishing work, Mystic Avenue bus/bike lanes, and plans to add roughly ten Bluebikes stations.

items.title: Wellington Station Air Rights Development
items.summary: The commission discussed potential transit-oriented development options for 28 acres of city-owned air rights at Wellington Station.

items.title: Bike Rack Funding and Bike Light Distribution
items.summary: The commission considered potential funding streams for public bike racks and noted ongoing distribution efforts for free bicycle light kits.

items.title: Bicycle Master Plan Update
items.summary: Lily outlined ongoing work mapping existing infrastructure, regional connections, and potential low-stress neighborway routes for the upcoming draft Master Plan.

items.title: World Day of Remembrance for Traffic Victims Announcement
items.summary: Ellery Klein announced that Walk Medford registered to observe the World Day of Remembrance for Traffic Victims in November.
